title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: In the giant Ni36Gd102 cluster, Ni is the CO2-binding site and μ3-OH− can supply protons for C–O cleavage, while Gd3+ is not the direct catalytic center but stabilizes the cluster and tunes the Ni2+ electronic structure and selectivity.
explanation: The soluble cluster, made by a mixed-ligand and sulfate-template route, adsorbs CO2 and photocatalytically reduces it to CO with 90.2% selectivity, TON 29700, and TOF 1.2 s−1. DFT indicates strong Ni–CO2 binding and hydrogen bonding between the cluster and CO2.
scope: High-nuclearity Ni–Gd coordination clusters for visible-light CO2-to-CO reduction.
conditions: λ > 420 nm, [Ru(phen)3](PF6)2, TEOA, CH3CN, 0.1 MPa, 1 h.
caveats: The Ln role is described for this cluster’s proposed cycle; it does not mean lanthanides are never the redox site in other LnCC CO2-reduction catalysts.
